rationale: The entry's core unifies the explicit definitional texts (John 4:34 with the Matt 12:50//Luke 8:21 equation of will and word-done, plus Ps 40:8) with the milk/meat contrast (Heb 5:14's 'by reason of use' and discernment; Job 34:3 tasting/trying; John 7:17) better than the common advanced-doctrine reading. The same-word-in-two-states claim accounts for the supplied details (received vs. carried to obedience) without contradiction, while the counter leaves John 4:34 as a disconnected alternative and underweights 'use'/obedience mechanics. No material assertion printed in the entry itself fails.
book_core_identification: Meat is the word of God carried through to complete obedience (the same word that, when merely received, is milk), thereby exercising the senses to discern.
book_secondary_elaborations: Meat exercises the senses to discern
chapter_only_objections: Extended claims that the gospel itself is meat only when obeyed (and milk when merely accepted), or that Christ-crucified is simultaneously milk and wisdom depending solely on the eater
Hebrew letter-play on chalav/cheleb (milk/fat) and basar (flesh/good tidings) plus preference for pre-Masoretic witnesses
Broader methodological assertions about every symbol being uniformly fixed across the canon or about semantic drift and AI analogies
strongest_counter_interpretation: Meat (solid food) symbolizes advanced or mature spiritual teaching and deeper doctrine suited to grown believers, in explicit contrast to milk as the elementary foundational teaching given to spiritual infants.
counter_core_identification: Meat is advanced/mature doctrinal content (solid food) for the spiritually mature, distinct from elementary milk content.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that meat is the identical word brought to complete obedience rather than a different, deeper body of teaching content.
counter_case: Heb 5:12-14 and 1 Cor 3:1-2 explicitly contrast milk for babes/unskilful who cannot bear meat with strong meat for the mature/full age
Heb 6:1-2 lists elementary doctrines as the foundation to be left, implying content progression
Traditional consensus across confessions reads the pair as levels of doctrinal depth rather than states of the same word
book_explanatory_advantages: Directly incorporates Jesus' own definitional sentence 'My meat is to do the will' (John 4:34) instead of isolating it as a separate metaphor
Explains the divine equation of 'do the will' = 'hear the word and do it' via the parallel Matt 12:50//Luke 8:21 plus Ps 40:8
Accounts for Heb 5:14's 'by reason of use' and discernment language, Job 34:3's tasting/trying, and John 7:17's obedience-to-knowledge link as the precise mechanism that turns milk into meat
Preserves the same substance (the word) across both states, matching the supplied John 6 bread-flesh-meat progression and 1 Cor 2-3 same-Christ-as-milk-or-wisdom observation
counter_explanatory_advantages: Matches the surface maturity-language and 'unable to bear it' phrasing in 1 Cor 3 and Heb 5 without additional steps
Aligns with the long-standing homiletic and commentary consensus that treats milk/meat as elementary vs. advanced content
